title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 4th draft of 'Analysis situs' (1986), Grothendieck axiomatizes an abstract 'space of figures', which he calls a 'magasin'. It consists of a set of elementary figures with three relations: a face/specialization relation <=, an 'interior incidence' relation (dotted <, written ≪, later denoted ◁) and a disjointness relation |∘|. A notion of support X ↦ |X| comes with an interior |X|^0. The previous page announced that the 'support axiom' is delicate. It is automatic when there is a fully faithful support function. The first test case is the magasins attached to ordered sets. This page treats case A.

Case A. Let L be totally ordered and dense ('divisible'): a<b implies ]a,b[ is nonempty.
- Define a set-theoretic ('ensembliste') magasin M inside the set of finite families of subsets of L (written 'Figil(L)' or similar). Its places (lieux) are the points of L.
- M = M_0 ⊔ M_1. Here M_0 = {P_x = {{x}} : x in L} are the points. M_1 = {S_{a,b} = {[a,b],{a},{b}} : a<b} are the closed segments together with their two endpoints.
- Axioms Mag 1 and 2 hold tautologically. M contains all the {{x}}, and M is stable under passing to sub-multistructures.

The relations, made explicit:
1) X <= Y iff X = Y, or X = P_x and Y = S_{a,b} with x in {a,b}. Equivalently ∂P_x = ∅ and ∂S_{a,b} = {P_a, P_b}. This is the face poset of a 1-dimensional cell structure.
2) X ≪ Y holds in three cases:
  (a) P_x ≪ P_y iff x = y;
  (b) P_x ≪ S_{a,b} iff a<x<b, i.e. x lies in the interior |S|^0 = ]a,b[;
  (c) S_{a,b} ≪ S_{a',b'} iff a' <= a < b <= b', i.e. |X| ⊂ |Y|, equivalently |X|^0 ⊂ |Y|^0 by density.

Consequence: the P_x are the minimal elements for <=. By density they are also the minimal elements for ≪, since every segment contains an interior point. Hence the 'lieux' are recovered intrinsically. The footnote says this holds for any magasin satisfying Mag 1 and 2.

Margin notes:
- Without density, one should only admit segments with ]a,b[ nonempty, so that S_{a,b} is a genuine figure with nonempty interior.
- Notation change: ◁ for ≪ and ⊴ for <=, with forward references to pp. 97–98.

The next page gives |∘|: interiors disjoint. It then passes to arbitrary posets (case B), where ≪ no longer matches support inclusion. That is where the predicted failure of the support axiom ('Oui!') is to come from.
errors: No substantive error. The equivalence |X| ⊂ |Y| ⟺ |X|^0 ⊂ |Y|^0 in (c) genuinely uses density and total order. This is implicitly acknowledged, and its failure for general posets is noted on the next page.
Minor: ≪ as defined is reflexive (P_x ≪ P_x, S ≪ S). So 'minimal for ≪' must be read as minimal for the strict part. The argument is fine under that reading.

ideas.what: Abstract 'magasin' of figures: a set with face relation <=, interior-incidence relation ≪, disjointness |∘|, and support/interior maps, as an axiomatic foundation for 'analysis situs' (tame topology).
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial/axiomatic tame topology; loosely abstract cell complexes, face posets, and point-free (mereotopological) frameworks
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tame topology programme: Grothendieck (Esquisse 1984); o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight; mereotopology: Whitehead, Clarke
ideas.where_published: Only the general wish for 'topologie modérée' appears in Esquisse d'un programme. The magasin axiomatics is in unpublished 1986 notes.

ideas.what: Magasin attached to a dense total order: points plus closed segments with endpoints, with interior incidence given by order intervals.
ideas.modern_name: 1-dimensional cell structure on a dense linear order (order topology / base case of o-minimal cell decomposition)

ideas.what: Places (lieux) recovered as minimal elements for ≪, which requires density, or alternatively Mag 1–2.
ideas.modern_name: Points as minimal elements / atoms in a point-free structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in point-free topology and mereotopology

missed.claim: The magasin axiomatics for analysis situs is an unpublished attempt at a combinatorial foundation of tame topology. Within it, ordered sets serve as the test case for when a 'support function' exists. The programme as a whole was never developed in the literature.
missed.quote: Magasin associé à un ensemble ordonné L ... Explicitons les relations ≤, ≪, |·|
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could be compared with o-minimal and point-free (locale/mereotopology) foundations. This page itself, however, is only a routine worked example.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine worked example: the order-interval model of a 1-dimensional figure structure. It is interesting only as part of the largely unknown 1986 magasin axiomatics. It contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: Title: 'Magasin associé à un ensemble ordonné L', not 'Megaris'.
'on va définir un magasin ensembliste' is likely, rather than 'une mégaris multistructurée'.
'les conditions Mag 1, 2 sont vérifiées', not 'M_0 [?] à M 1, 2'.
Margin NB likely reads roughly: 'Quand on n'admet pas la divisibilité, il convient de prendre pour S_ab seulement les a<b tels que ]a,b[≠∅, i.e. S°_{ab} ≠ ∅' (to make S_ab a genuine figure).
Second margin NB: 'X ◁ Y pour X ≪ Y et X ⊴ Y pour X ≤ Y', with references to pp. 97, 98.
